**2. Complete the following text below so that it should make sense. (5 marks)**

**Man dies in a Hotel**

A man in his fifties was found dead in a hotel. It is said that the man was an……………. (1) of an insurance company in Yaoundé. He had ……………. (2) into the hotel the ……………. (3) evening and asked for a quiet room. The cleaner who went into the room early the ……………. (4) morning to clean it was surprised that the door was locked at mid day. She banged on the door ……………. (5) but to no avail. Then she called the receptionist and, ……………. (6) they tried to push open the door. As they opened it they were ……………. (7) to see their customer lying in bed without any signs of ……………. (8)

They at once called the police. A doctor came round and said the man probably had a heart ……………. (9) His corpse was taken to a local hospital for a……………. (10) mortem examination. There are wild rumours about the cause of the death. Some people say he was poisoned; others say he was the victim of a tug of love.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Ce texte à trous raconte un fait divers : chaque mot manquant doit rester cohérent avec la logique narrative et policière du récit (arrivée à l'hôtel, découverte du corps, intervention de la police, cause du décès encore incertaine). Le vocabulaire attendu appartient au registre du fait divers et de l'enquête.

### Rappel de méthode
Ce texte à trous raconte un fait divers : chaque mot manquant doit rester cohérent avec la logique narrative et policière du récit (arrivée à l'hôtel, découverte du corps, intervention de la police, cause du décès encore incertaine). Le vocabulaire attendu appartient au registre du fait divers et de l'enquête.

**Texte complété (les mots ajoutés sont en gras) :**

A man in his fifties was found dead in a hotel. It is said that the man was an **employee** of an insurance company in Yaoundé. He had **checked** into the hotel the **previous** evening and asked for a quiet room. The cleaner who went into the room early the **following** morning to clean it was surprised that the door was locked at mid day. She banged on the door **repeatedly** but to no avail. Then she called the receptionist and, **together**, they tried to push open the door. As they opened it they were **shocked** to see their customer lying in bed without any signs of **life**.

They at once called the police. A doctor came round and said the man probably had a heart **attack**. His corpse was taken to a local hospital for a **post** mortem examination. There are wild rumours about the cause of the death. Some people say he was poisoned; others say he was the victim of a tug of love.

Chaque mot ajouté s'appuie sur un repère temporel ou narratif du texte : « previous evening » et « following morning » marquent la chronologie de l'arrivée puis de la découverte, tandis que « post mortem » reprend l'expression figée médico-légale que la suite du mot (« mortem ») indique déjà à moitié.

### Piège à éviter
Le blanc (8) doit rester cohérent avec la suite du texte : compléter par un mot comme « movement » plutôt que « life » resterait grammaticalement correct mais affaiblirait la gravité de la scène découverte, qui doit annoncer clairement une personne morte, non simplement immobile.

### Conseil
Pour ce type de texte narratif à trous, repère d'abord les deux réactions-clés du texte (la surprise de la femme de ménage, le choc à l'ouverture de la porte) : elles orientent fortement le choix des mots environnants, notamment vers un vocabulaire de mort et non de simple sommeil.
